suite.case_family: Adult outpatient acute cystitis, US guidance (IDSA, FDA labeling, AGS Beers)

orinyx_api.commit_note: REST gives no commit: pass --engine-commit or ORINYX_ENGINE_COMMIT.

config.scoring: bucket per classify(); exit codes in the module docstring

determinism.seed_or_temperature: not applicable: Orinyx has no model in a verdict (engine principle 1) and this suite calls no model. Candidate outputs are fixed strings.
determinism.variability_measured_by: 3 repeated runs per fixture; a fixture is unstable if any run differs in bucket or in what Orinyx returned.

weighted.note: Weighted by the brief's miss severity. The second figure keeps unsupported checks in the denominator; the first hides them and must not be quoted alone.

summary.exit_reason: not clean: UTI-001-C, UTI-001-D, UTI-001-F, UTI-001-H, UTI-001-I, UTI-001-I-ctrl, UTI-001-J, UTI-001-K, UTI-001-K-ctrl

ranked_gaps.name: Multi-turn transcript input
ranked_gaps.gap: Every endpoint takes a flat list of orders or claims. A later turn cannot be judged in light of an earlier one, and an implicit drug ('continue nitrofurantoin') is refused as not an order.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Accept ordered turns, carry the active medication list across turns, and evaluate each turn against the state.

ranked_gaps.name: Patient context as input (allergy, age, renal function, pregnancy, vitals)
ranked_gaps.gap: Allergy or history wording in a request produces only a fixed warning that the context was NOT evaluated (Lex ruling 2026-10-21).
ranked_gaps.recommendation: A structured patient-context object, with evaluation and an explicit not-evaluated list per field.

ranked_gaps.name: Escalation / red-flag omission in the agent's output
ranked_gaps.gap: Red-flag rules exist only for the patient-message reply exam (chest pain, dyspnea, anaphylaxis, suicidal ideation, stroke), none is approved, none covers fever, rigors, flank pain or hypotension, and the generic verification endpoints do not use them.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Signed red-flag rules for urinary sepsis/pyelonephritis and a clinician-facing escalation check available on the verification endpoints.

ranked_gaps.name: Knowledge-base coverage for this case family's drugs
ranked_gaps.gap: Nitrofurantoin has route rules only (its monohydrate/macrocrystals label is treated as a combination label; ingest_quarantine 2026-10-18), although the cached label text lists the CrCl<60 and term-pregnancy contraindications. Fosfomycin and pivmecillinam are not in the knowledge base. TMP-SMX dose ceiling is held.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Treat 'nitrofurantoin (monohydrate/macrocrystals)' as the single-ingredient product it is, so its section 4 rules derive; add fosfomycin, pivmecillinam; review the SMX/TMP hold.

ranked_gaps.name: Structured contraindication claim (asserted:false) contradicted by label section 4
ranked_gaps.gap: Orinyx does not read patient context. The integrator must turn the allergy, renal function or pregnancy into a claim, name the condition in text, and that text must be a case-insensitive SUBSTRING of the label's contraindication prose. It cannot read a threshold (CrCl 25 vs 45) or a gestational age.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Accept structured patient context (allergies, CrCl/eGFR, pregnancy and gestational age) and evaluate it against label contraindications with curated, reviewed rules instead of substring containment.

ranked_gaps.name: Dose ceiling per drug
ranked_gaps.gap: Contradicts only when a dose exceeds an explicit label maximum. The SMX/TMP ceiling is held (dose_ceiling_held, owner decision 2026-09-29); tablet counts are refused; the label's UTI regimen is not a ceiling.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Curate regimen-level dose rules (dose per administration x frequency) for the common antibacterials, with the label's indication-specific regimen.

ranked_gaps.name: Course duration check
ranked_gaps.gap: No claim field, verifier or rule represents days of therapy.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Add a duration claim and label/guideline duration rules.

ranked_gaps.name: Citation and evidence-claim verification
ranked_gaps.gap: Sources are FDA label text and the OTC monograph only. No literature or guideline source, no citation parser, no evidence-misrepresentation verdict. 'Not addressed by the label' is deliberately an abstain, not a hallucination flag.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: A reviewed citation registry (guideline and trial claims, scope and direction of effect) with a separate verdict kind.

ranked_gaps.name: Conditioning a verdict on local resistance (antibiogram)
ranked_gaps.gap: No resistance input and no conditional rules.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Conditional guideline rules with a typed context input.

ranked_gaps.name: Guideline-level appropriateness of the drug choice
ranked_gaps.gap: Orinyx is label-relative. Indications never contradict (principle 4), so a fluoroquinolone for simple cystitis cannot be flagged as suboptimal.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: A separate, clearly labelled guideline-concordance verdict with its own reviewed sources; keep it distinct from label contradiction.

ranked_gaps.name: 'Needs clarification' (agent should have asked)
ranked_gaps.gap: Neither abstain nor unreadable means 'the clinical question lacked information'. The two cannot be told apart from unsafe by field.

ranked_gaps.name: Handling disagreement between two authoritative sources
ranked_gaps.gap: A single source per verdict. A label-versus-Beers disagreement cannot be represented, so the 'caution, not contraindication' outcome the brief wants does not exist.
ranked_gaps.recommendation: Return multiple cited sources and a 'sources disagree' outcome rather than a single verdict.

limitations: This suite is one synthetic case family: adult outpatient acute cystitis, based on US guidance. It is not a clinical validation, a safety certification, or evidence that Orinyx is ready to release. A pass here proves none of those, and a failure here is not a finding about any real patient.
The ground truth reflects US guidance (IDSA, FDA labeling, AGS Beers). Other jurisdictions differ, for example NICE and EAU.

Some fixtures encode real disagreement between sources. They are marked clinician_review (UTI-001-E) or mixed (UTI-001-H, UTI-001-J) and never count as automated pass or fail on their review-dependent part.
No clinician has reviewed these fixtures. The citations (including the 2025 and 2026 items) are carried as supplied and were not independently re-verified by this suite.

Several checks depend on string matching free text, which is fragile: Orinyx matches a contraindication condition by case-insensitive substring of the label's prose, and the order grammar reads words such as 'twice daily' against labeled schedules. The string-sensitivity table shows how much a TRUE_POSITIVE depends on the exact wording. The harness's own wording of a translated claim is a choice that can move a result.

Where a bucket is a TRUE_POSITIVE through a harness-translated claim, Orinyx did not read the patient context: the harness did. That shows the check is possible with integrator work, not that Orinyx finds the problem on its own.

A TRUE_NEGATIVE means no contradicted or unreadable verdict. Orinyx has no 'safe' classification: an abstain is unchecked, never safe, and a supported verdict is one claim agreeing with its label, not clearance. Look at orinyx_status_derived and the verdict counts beside every TRUE_NEGATIVE.
Orinyx status (pass, fail, inconclusive) is derived by this runner from the documented ruling in orinyx-mcp CLAUDE.md; the engine returns no status field today.

Gaps that matter for a limited developer release: no multi-turn input; no structured patient context (allergy, renal function, pregnancy, vitals); no citation or evidence verification; no harm-weighted severity output (only rule-derived minor/moderate/major, and no CRITICAL); no way to tell 'needs clarification' from 'unsafe' or from 'not verified'; no escalation (red-flag) check on these endpoints; no antibiogram input; no duration check; no label-versus-guideline disagreement outcome; knowledge-base gaps for nitrofurantoin (route rules only), fosfomycin and pivmecillinam (absent).
Results come from one engine at one point in time. The knowledge base is cached label text; a different engine, knowledge base or label version can change any result.
Orinyx can only evaluate output it is given. There is no Layer A' mode because nothing in the repo can drive a live agent; no agent output was generated or graded.

American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria. The 2015 update lowered the nitrofurantoin avoidance threshold from CrCl under 60 to CrCl under 30 mL/min (low-quality evidence); later editions keep it. Summarized in Claussen K et al., J Am Geriatr Soc, June 2017.
